claim: The development of neurons in the peripheral nervous system is dependent on target-derived, long-range retrograde neurotrophic factor signals.
source: The development of neurons in the peripheral nervous system is dependent on target-derived, long-range retrograde neurotrophic factor signals.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that represents established knowledge in the field of neuroscience.

claim: The prevailing view is that target-derived nerve growth factor (NGF) and its receptor TrkA are carried retrogradely by early endosomes.
source: The prevailing view is that target-derived nerve growth factor (NGF), the prototypical neurotrophin, and its receptor TrkA are carried retrogradely by early endosomes, which serve as TrkA signaling platforms in cell bodies.
evidence: This statement describes the existing scientific consensus prior to the current study.

claim: The majority of retrograde TrkA signaling endosomes in mouse sympathetic neurons are ultrastructurally and molecularly defined multivesicular bodies (MVBs).
source: Here, we report that the majority of retrograde TrkA signaling endosomes in mouse sympathetic neurons are ultrastructurally and molecularly defined multivesicular bodies (MVBs).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Retrogradely transported TrkA+ MVBs that arrive in cell bodies evade lysosomal fusion.
source: In contrast to MVBs that carry non-TrkA cargoes from distal axons to cell bodies, retrogradely transported TrkA+ MVBs that arrive in cell bodies evade lysosomal fusion and instead evolve into TrkA+ single-membrane vesicles that are signaling competent.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing differential fates of TrkA+ versus non-TrkA+ MVBs.

claim: Retrogradely transported TrkA+ MVBs evolve into TrkA+ single-membrane vesicles that are signaling competent.
source: In contrast to MVBs that carry non-TrkA cargoes from distal axons to cell bodies, retrogradely transported TrkA+ MVBs that arrive in cell bodies evade lysosomal fusion and instead evolve into TrkA+ single-membrane vesicles that are signaling competent.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on ultrastructural and molecular analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: TrkA kinase activity associated with retrogradely transported TrkA+ MVBs determines TrkA+ endosome evolution and fate.
source: Moreover, TrkA kinase activity associated with retrogradely transported TrkA+ MVBs determines TrkA+ endosome evolution and fate.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by chemical genetic experiments manipulating TrkA kinase activity.

claim: MVBs deliver long-range retrograde NGF signals and serve as signaling and sorting platforms in the cell soma.
source: Thus, MVBs deliver long-range retrograde NGF signals and serve as signaling and sorting platforms in the cell soma, and MVB cargoes dictate their vesicular fate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: MVB cargoes dictate their vesicular fate.
source: Thus, MVBs deliver long-range retrograde NGF signals and serve as signaling and sorting platforms in the cell soma, and MVB cargoes dictate their vesicular fate.
evidence: This conclusion is based on data showing differential fates of TrkA+ versus non-TrkA+ MVBs.

claim: Developing neurons in the peripheral nervous system are critically dependent on target-derived trophic cues released by the end organs they innervate.
source: Developing neurons in the peripheral nervous system (PNS) are critically dependent on target-derived trophic cues released by the end organs they innervate.
evidence: This is established knowledge in developmental neuroscience.

claim: The neurotrophin family of growth factors includes nerve growth factor (NGF), brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), neurotrophin-3 (NT3) and neurotrophin-4 (NT4).
source: This is best exemplified for primary somatosensory neurons and postganglionic sympathetic neurons and their dependence on members of the neurotrophin family of growth factors, which includes nerve growth factor (NGF), brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), neurotrophin-3 (NT3) and neurotrophin-4 (NT4).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the neurotrophin family.

claim: NGF binds to and activates TrkA receptor.
source: Through binding to and activating their cognate receptors (NGF to TrkA, BDNF and NT4 to TrkB, NT3 predominantly to TrkC), neurotrophins promote neuronal survival, axonal growth and target field innervation, neuronal subtype specification and, for sympathetic neurons, synapse formation and maintenance (Cosker et al., 2008; Harrington and Ginty, 2013; Huang and Reichardt, 2001; Luo et al., 2007; Miller and Kaplan, 2001; Sharma et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: BDNF and NT4 bind to and activate TrkB receptor.
source: Through binding to and activating their cognate receptors (NGF to TrkA, BDNF and NT4 to TrkB, NT3 predominantly to TrkC), neurotrophins promote neuronal survival, axonal growth and target field innervation, neuronal subtype specification and, for sympathetic neurons, synapse formation and maintenance (Cosker et al., 2008; Harrington and Ginty, 2013; Huang and Reichardt, 2001; Luo et al., 2007; Miller and Kaplan, 2001; Sharma et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: NT3 predominantly binds to and activates TrkC receptor.
source: Through binding to and activating their cognate receptors (NGF to TrkA, BDNF and NT4 to TrkB, NT3 predominantly to TrkC), neurotrophins promote neuronal survival, axonal growth and target field innervation, neuronal subtype specification and, for sympathetic neurons, synapse formation and maintenance (Cosker et al., 2008; Harrington and Ginty, 2013; Huang and Reichardt, 2001; Luo et al., 2007; Miller and Kaplan, 2001; Sharma et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Neurotrophins promote neuronal survival, axonal growth and target field innervation, neuronal subtype specification and synapse formation and maintenance.
source: Through binding to and activating their cognate receptors (NGF to TrkA, BDNF and NT4 to TrkB, NT3 predominantly to TrkC), neurotrophins promote neuronal survival, axonal growth and target field innervation, neuronal subtype specification and, for sympathetic neurons, synapse formation and maintenance (Cosker et al., 2008; Harrington and Ginty, 2013; Huang and Reichardt, 2001; Luo et al., 2007; Miller and Kaplan, 2001; Sharma et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: NGF is the first described and prototypical neurotrophin.
source: NGF is the first described and prototypical neurotrophin.
evidence: This is a historical fact about NGF discovery.

claim: The NGF/TrkA signal must be propagated retrogradely from distal axons to the soma to elicit trophic actions on developing sensory and sympathetic neurons.
source: A remarkable feature of NGF signaling is that, in order to elicit trophic actions on developing sensory and sympathetic neurons, the NGF/TrkA signal must be propagated retrogradely, from distal axons to the soma, traveling a distance that is thousands of times the diameter of the cell body (Cosker et al., 2008; Howe and Mobley, 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The NGF/TrkA signal travels a distance that is thousands of times the diameter of the cell body.
source: A remarkable feature of NGF signaling is that, in order to elicit trophic actions on developing sensory and sympathetic neurons, the NGF/TrkA signal must be propagated retrogradely, from distal axons to the soma, traveling a distance that is thousands of times the diameter of the cell body (Cosker et al., 2008; Howe and Mobley, 2005).
evidence: This is a quantitative description of the distance of retrograde transport supported by citations.

claim: The molecular events that orchestrate long-range axonal NGF signaling remain unclear and debated.
source: Although much is known about downstream signaling pathways and transcriptional targets that mediate the trophic actions of NGF, the molecular events that orchestrate this unique form of long-range axonal signaling remain unclear and debated.
evidence: This statement describes the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: A major mode of retrograde NGF signal propagation is through the actions of NGF/TrkA signaling endosomes.
source: A major mode of retrograde NGF signal propagation is through the actions of NGF/TrkA signaling endosomes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about NGF signaling mechanisms.

claim: The signaling endosome model posits that NGF/TrkA complexes formed at distal axons are internalized and actively sorted into endosomes.
source: The signaling endosome model posits that NGF/TrkA complexes formed at distal axons are internalized and actively sorted into endosomes, a subset of which become mature, signaling-competent vesicles that undergo long-distance, microtubule-mediated retrograde transport to the soma (Howe and Mobley, 2005; Ye et al., 2003; Heerssen et al., 2004; Wu et al., 2007).
evidence: This describes an existing model in the field supported by citations.

claim: A subset of NGF/TrkA endosomes become mature, signaling-competent vesicles that undergo long-distance, microtubule-mediated retrograde transport to the soma.
source: The signaling endosome model posits that NGF/TrkA complexes formed at distal axons are internalized and actively sorted into endosomes, a subset of which become mature, signaling-competent vesicles that undergo long-distance, microtubule-mediated retrograde transport to the soma (Howe and Mobley, 2005; Ye et al., 2003; Heerssen et al., 2004; Wu et al., 2007).
evidence: This describes an existing model supported by citations.

claim: TrkA receptors labeled in distal axons prior to internalization subsequently appear in proximal axons, cell bodies and dendrites of sympathetic neurons in vitro.
source: Indeed, experiments in which TrkA receptors were labeled in distal axons prior to internalization revealed their subsequent appearance in proximal axons, cell bodies and dendrites of sympathetic neurons in vitro (Sharma et al., 2010; Harrington et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a finding from previous studies supported by citations.

claim: TrkA endosomes in different cellular compartments can function as signaling platforms that propagate trophic signals to support survival, maturation, and synapse formation and maintenance.
source: By recruiting TrkA effectors, TrkA endosomes in these different cellular compartments can function as signaling platforms that propagate trophic signals to support survival, maturation, and synapse formation and maintenance (Heerssen et al., 2004; Harrington et al., 2011; Howe et al., 2001; Suo et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: A long-standing, canonical view is that retrograde NGF/TrkA signaling endosomes are early endosomes.
source: A long-standing, canonical view is that retrograde NGF/TrkA signaling endosomes are early endosomes because, like other ligand/receptor complexes, internalized NGF/TrkA complexes are sorted into early endosomes and the membrane topology of receptors in early endosome-type vesicles can, in principle, enable signal propagation within the cytoplasm (Cosker et al., 2008; Harrington and Ginty, 2013; Howe and Mobley, 2005).
evidence: This describes the prevailing view in the field supported by citations.

claim: Internalized NGF/TrkA complexes are sorted into early endosomes.
source: A long-standing, canonical view is that retrograde NGF/TrkA signaling endosomes are early endosomes because, like other ligand/receptor complexes, internalized NGF/TrkA complexes are sorted into early endosomes and the membrane topology of receptors in early endosome-type vesicles can, in principle, enable signal propagation within the cytoplasm (Cosker et al., 2008; Harrington and Ginty, 2013; Howe and Mobley, 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Rab5 is enriched in purified axoplasmic fractions that contained retrograde 125I-NGF.
source: The small GTPase Rab5, a molecular marker and master regulator of early endosomes (Zerial and McBride, 2001), is enriched in purified axoplasmic fractions that contained retrograde 125I-NGF.
evidence: This is a finding from previous studies supported by citations.

claim: Rab5 is a molecular marker and master regulator of early endosomes.
source: The small GTPase Rab5, a molecular marker and master regulator of early endosomes (Zerial and McBride, 2001), is enriched in purified axoplasmic fractions that contained retrograde 125I-NGF.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: TrkA was found associated with single-membrane vesicles labeled by Rab5.
source: Also, TrkA was found associated with single-membrane vesicles labeled by Rab5 (Delcroix et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a finding from a previous study supported by a citation.

claim: Retrogradely transported NGF conjugated to quantum dots was colocalized with Rab5 in compartmentalized cultures of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons.
source: In agreement with this, retrogradely transported NGF conjugated to quantum dots was colocalized with Rab5 in compartmentalized cultures of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons (Cui et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a finding from a previous study supported by a citation.

claim: Late endosomes (LEs) and multi-vesicular bodies (MVBs) have been observed to contain retrogradely transported cargoes in other experimental paradigms.
source: However, despite the widely accepted view that signaling endosomes are early endosomes, late endosomes (LEs) and multi-vesicular bodies (MVBs) have been observed to contain retrogradely transported cargoes in other experimental paradigms.
evidence: This statement describes findings from other studies that contradict the prevailing view.

claim: In cultured DRG and motor neurons, internalized tetanus toxin is sorted into TrkB+ vesicles associated with either Rab5 or Rab7 within axons.
source: For example, in cultured DRG and motor neurons, internalized tetanus toxin is sorted into TrkB+ vesicles associated with either Rab5 or Rab7 (a small GTPase enriched in MVBs and LEs) within axons, but only Rab7+ vesicles underwent long-range retrograde transport (Deinhardt et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a finding from a previous study supported by a citation.

claim: Only Rab7+ vesicles underwent long-range retrograde transport of tetanus toxin in cultured DRG and motor neurons.
source: For example, in cultured DRG and motor neurons, internalized tetanus toxin is sorted into TrkB+ vesicles associated with either Rab5 or Rab7 (a small GTPase enriched in MVBs and LEs) within axons, but only Rab7+ vesicles underwent long-range retrograde transport (Deinhardt et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a finding from a previous study supported by a citation.

claim: Rab7 is a small GTPase enriched in MVBs and LEs.
source: For example, in cultured DRG and motor neurons, internalized tetanus toxin is sorted into TrkB+ vesicles associated with either Rab5 or Rab7 (a small GTPase enriched in MVBs and LEs) within axons, but only Rab7+ vesicles underwent long-range retrograde transport (Deinhardt et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: In compartmentalized sympathetic neuron cultures, 125I-NGF applied to distal axons was found predominantly in MVBs and lysosomes based on ultrastructural analysis.
source: In addition, in compartmentalized sympathetic neuron cultures, 125I-NGF applied to distal axons was found predominantly in MVBs and lysosomes, based on ultrastructural analysis (Claude et al., 1982a, 1982b).
evidence: This is a finding from previous studies supported by citations.

claim: Gold-labeled NGF injected into the anterior chamber of the eye accumulated in MVBs in axons near sympathetic ganglia.
source: In related work, gold-labeled NGF injected into the anterior chamber of the eye accumulated in MVBs in axons near sympathetic ganglia (Sandow et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a finding from a previous study supported by a citation.

claim: Activated TrkA was observed in multivesicular structures in the rat sciatic nerve.
source: Also, activated TrkA was observed in multivesicular structures in the rat sciatic nerve (Bhattacharyya et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a finding from a previous study supported by a citation.

claim: BDNF injected into the tongue did not appear associated with MVBs or any other ultrastructurally defined endosome type in hypoglossal motor neurons.
source: However, BDNF injected into the tongue did not appear associated with MVBs or any other ultrastructurally defined endosome type in hypoglossal motor neurons (Altick et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a finding from a previous study supported by a citation.

claim: There is a lack of a plausible mechanism to explain how signals emanating from NGF/TrkA complexes encapsulated within intraluminal vesicles of MVBs are transmitted to the cytoplasm.
source: Moreover, a key conceptual challenge to the idea that MVBs are TrkA signal carriers is the lack of a plausible mechanism to explain how signals emanating from NGF/TrkA complexes encapsulated within intraluminal vesicles of MVBs are transmitted to the cytoplasm.
evidence: This describes a conceptual challenge in the field.

claim: Molecularly and ultrastructurally defined MVBs carry the majority of NGF/TrkA complexes from distal axons to cell bodies.
source: Here, we demonstrate that molecularly and ultrastructurally defined MVBs carry the majority of NGF/TrkA complexes from distal axons to cell bodies.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Rab7 is essential in vivo and in vitro for retrograde TrkA signaling.
source: Moreover, Rab7, which regulates MVB and LE function (Zerial and McBride, 2001; Vanlandingham and Ceresa, 2009; Lebrand et al., 2002), is essential in vivo and in vitro for retrograde TrkA signaling.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Rab7 regulates MVB and LE function.
source: Moreover, Rab7, which regulates MVB and LE function (Zerial and McBride, 2001; Vanlandingham and Ceresa, 2009; Lebrand et al., 2002), is essential in vivo and in vitro for retrograde TrkA signaling.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: TrkA+ MVBs that arrive in cell bodies do not fuse with lysosomes.
source: Strikingly, TrkA+ MVBs that arrive in cell bodies do not fuse with lysosomes, but rather can give rise to single-membrane vesicles marked by Vps35, but not Rab5.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: TrkA+ MVBs can give rise to single-membrane vesicles marked by Vps35, but not Rab5.
source: Strikingly, TrkA+ MVBs that arrive in cell bodies do not fuse with lysosomes, but rather can give rise to single-membrane vesicles marked by Vps35, but not Rab5.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: TrkA kinase activity controls the maturation and fate of TrkA+ MVBs.
source: Moreover, TrkA kinase activity controls the maturation and fate of TrkA+ MVBs.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: MVBs are mediators of long-range retrograde TrkA signaling.
source: Thus, MVBs are mediators of long-range retrograde TrkA signaling, evading lysosomal fusion and degradation within the soma in a TrkA kinase-dependent manner, and evolving within the soma into single membrane vesicles with the capacity to propagate TrkA survival signals.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: MVBs evade lysosomal fusion and degradation within the soma in a TrkA kinase-dependent manner.
source: Thus, MVBs are mediators of long-range retrograde TrkA signaling, evading lysosomal fusion and degradation within the soma in a TrkA kinase-dependent manner, and evolving within the soma into single membrane vesicles with the capacity to propagate TrkA survival signals.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental findings.

claim: MVBs evolve within the soma into single membrane vesicles with the capacity to propagate TrkA survival signals.
source: Thus, MVBs are mediators of long-range retrograde TrkA signaling, evading lysosomal fusion and degradation within the soma in a TrkA kinase-dependent manner, and evolving within the soma into single membrane vesicles with the capacity to propagate TrkA survival signals.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental findings.

claim: Application of anti-Flag antibody pre-conjugated to Protein A-5nm gold to distal axons of compartmentalized Ntrk1Flag neurons labeled electron dense structures in axons.
source: While application of neither the primary antibody nor Protein A-5nm gold alone to distal axons of compartmentalized Ntrk1Flag neurons yielded electron-dense structures detectable by EM, application of anti-Flag antibody that was pre-conjugated to Protein A-5nm gold to Ntrk1Flag neurons, but not wild-type neurons, labeled electron dense structures in axons that were readily apparent by EM (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a methodological finding supported by experimental data and Figure 1A.

claim: Gold-labeled TrkA receptors did not compromise survival or retrograde signaling.
source: This antibody labeling strategy did not perturb normal internalization and endocytic trafficking of TrkA receptors; Gold-labeled TrkA receptors did not compromise survival or retrograde signaling (data not shown), nor did it affect the subcellular and ultrastructural localization of P-TrkA, visualized by either light microscopy or EM (see below, Figures 4 and 6).
evidence: This is a control finding validating the experimental method.

claim: Gold labeling did not affect the subcellular and ultrastructural localization of P-TrkA.
source: This antibody labeling strategy did not perturb normal internalization and endocytic trafficking of TrkA receptors; Gold-labeled TrkA receptors did not compromise survival or retrograde signaling (data not shown), nor did it affect the subcellular and ultrastructural localization of P-TrkA, visualized by either light microscopy or EM (see below, Figures 4 and 6).
evidence: This is a control finding supported by data in Figures 4 and 6.

claim: Newly internalized, gold-labeled TrkA receptors in distal axons were found in single-membrane vesicular structures in close proximity to the plasma membrane.
source: As expected, newly internalized, gold-labeled TrkA receptors in distal axons were found in single-membrane vesicular structures in close proximity to the plasma membrane, which is a defining feature of early endosomes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Retrogradely transported TrkA receptors in proximal axons and cell bodies were found mainly in MVBs (87.9 ± 5.0%).
source: Surprisingly, and in stark contrast, retrogradely transported TrkA receptors in proximal axons and cell bodies were found mainly in MVBs (87.9 ± 5.0%) and, to a much lesser extent, single-membrane vesicles (SVs, 9.5 ± 2.8%) or lysosomes (2.6 ± 1.3%; Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from EM analysis supported by Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Retrogradely transported TrkA receptors in proximal axons and cell bodies were found in single-membrane vesicles (9.5 ± 2.8%).
source: Surprisingly, and in stark contrast, retrogradely transported TrkA receptors in proximal axons and cell bodies were found mainly in MVBs (87.9 ± 5.0%) and, to a much lesser extent, single-membrane vesicles (SVs, 9.5 ± 2.8%) or lysosomes (2.6 ± 1.3%; Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from EM analysis supported by Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Retrogradely transported TrkA receptors in proximal axons and cell bodies were found in lysosomes (2.6 ± 1.3%).
source: Surprisingly, and in stark contrast, retrogradely transported TrkA receptors in proximal axons and cell bodies were found mainly in MVBs (87.9 ± 5.0%) and, to a much lesser extent, single-membrane vesicles (SVs, 9.5 ± 2.8%) or lysosomes (2.6 ± 1.3%; Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from EM analysis supported by Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Gold-labeled Flag-TrkA receptors were localized both to the limiting membrane and intraluminal vesicles (ILVs) of MVBs.
source: The gold-labeled Flag-TrkA receptors were localized both to the limiting membrane and intraluminal vesicles (ILVs) of MVBs (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by Figure 1B.

claim: Following NGF treatment of distal axons, newly internalized TrkA in distal axons is associated with early endosomes.
source: Therefore, following NGF treatment of distal axons, newly internalized TrkA in distal axons is associated with early endosomes, whereas following retrograde transport to proximal axons and cell bodies TrkA is predominantly associated with MVBs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the EM analysis data.

claim: Following retrograde transport to proximal axons and cell bodies, TrkA is predominantly associated with MVBs.
source: Therefore, following NGF treatment of distal axons, newly internalized TrkA in distal axons is associated with early endosomes, whereas following retrograde transport to proximal axons and cell bodies TrkA is predominantly associated with MVBs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the EM analysis data.

claim: Following application of NGF exclusively to distal axons, newly internalized TrkA receptors in distal axons were mainly associated with Rab5-labeled early endosomes.
source: Consistent with the EM observations, following application of NGF exclusively to distal axons, newly internalized TrkA receptors in distal axons were mainly associated with Rab5-labeled early endosomes (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by Figure 2A.

claim: The fraction of total internalized Flag-TrkA colocalized with Rab5 in distal axons decreased during the next hour.
source: However, the fraction of total internalized Flag-TrkA colocalized with Rab5 in distal axons decreased during the next hour, coincident with an increase of Flag-TrkA colocalized with Rab7, a small GTPase that regulates the functions of MVBs and late endosomes (LEs) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) (Vanlandingham and Ceresa, 2009; Lebrand et al., 2002).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The fraction of total internalized Flag-TrkA colocalized with Rab7 in distal axons increased during the hour following NGF application.
source: However, the fraction of total internalized Flag-TrkA colocalized with Rab5 in distal axons decreased during the next hour, coincident with an increase of Flag-TrkA colocalized with Rab7, a small GTPase that regulates the functions of MVBs and late endosomes (LEs) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) (Vanlandingham and Ceresa, 2009; Lebrand et al., 2002).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Flag-TrkA punctae within proximal axons were mainly associated with MVB/LE markers, including Rab7, Hrs and CD63.
source: Strikingly, Flag-TrkA punctae within proximal axons, which represent mature, retrogradely transported endosomes, were mainly associated with MVB/LE markers, including Rab7, Hrs (Henne et al., 2011) and CD63 (Pols and Klumperman, 2009) and, to a much lesser extent, with markers of early endosomes (Rab5), recycling endosomes (Rab11) and lysosomes (Lamp1) (Figure 2A,B; Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Flag-TrkA punctae within proximal axons were associated to a much lesser extent with markers of early endosomes (Rab5), recycling endosomes (Rab11) and lysosomes (Lamp1).
source: Strikingly, Flag-TrkA punctae within proximal axons, which represent mature, retrogradely transported endosomes, were mainly associated with MVB/LE markers, including Rab7, Hrs (Henne et al., 2011) and CD63 (Pols and Klumperman, 2009) and, to a much lesser extent, with markers of early endosomes (Rab5), recycling endosomes (Rab11) and lysosomes (Lamp1) (Figure 2A,B; Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: The majority of EGFP-Rab5+/Flag-TrkA endosomes in distal axons are stationary or move bi-directionally for only a short distance.
source: Live cell imaging of EGFP-Rab5-expressing Ntrk1Flag neurons revealed that the majority of EGFP-Rab5+/Flag-TrkA endosomes in distal axons are stationary or move bi-directionally for only a short distance (Figure 2C, yellow arrow heads).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from live cell imaging supported by Figure 2C.

claim: Only few of the EGFP-Rab5+/Flag-TrkA+ punctae were co-transported retrogradely into proximal axons of the cell body compartment.
source: Consistent with this, only few of the EGFP-Rab5+/Flag-TrkA+ punctae were co-transported retrogradely into proximal axons of the cell body compartment (Figure 2C–E; Video 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from live cell imaging supported by Figure 2C–E and Video 1.

claim: The majority of retrogradely transported Flag-TrkA+ endosomes observed within proximal axons were associated with EGFP-Rab7.
source: In contrast, the majority of retrogradely transported Flag-TrkA+ endosomes observed within proximal axons were associated with EGFP-Rab7 (Figure 2C, white arrow heads).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from live cell imaging supported by Figure 2C.

claim: The majority of EGFP-Rab7+ TrkA endosomes exhibited processive movement in the retrograde direction.
source: Furthermore, unlike EGFP-Rab5+/Flag-TrkA+ endosomes, the majority of EGFP-Rab7+ TrkA endosomes exhibited processive movement in the retrograde direction; very few were stationary or moved bi-directionally (Figure 2C–E; Video 2).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from live cell imaging supported by Figure 2C–E and Video 2.

claim: Very few EGFP-Rab7+ TrkA endosomes were stationary or moved bi-directionally.
source: Furthermore, unlike EGFP-Rab5+/Flag-TrkA+ endosomes, the majority of EGFP-Rab7+ TrkA endosomes exhibited processive movement in the retrograde direction; very few were stationary or moved bi-directionally (Figure 2C–E; Video 2).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from live cell imaging supported by Figure 2C–E and Video 2.

claim: The percentages of Flag-TrkA punctae co-transported with either EGFP-Rab5 or EGFP-Rab7 were similar to the percentages of colocalization observed in the fixed cell immunolabeling experiments.
source: The percentages of Flag-TrkA punctae co-transported with either EGFP-Rab5 or EGFP-Rab7 were similar to the percentages of colocalization observed in the fixed cell immunolabeling experiments.
evidence: This is a comparison between live cell imaging and fixed cell data.

claim: The majority of retrograde Flag-TrkA+ endosomes are associated with markers of MVBs or LEs, and not early endosomes.
source: These observations, taken together, demonstrate that the majority of retrograde Flag-TrkA+ endosomes are associated with markers of MVBs or LEs, and not early endosomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: Th2a-CreER; Rab7f/f animals exhibited ~60% neuronal cell loss compared to Th2a-CreER; Rab7+/+ littermate controls.
source: Compared to Th2a-CreER; Rab7+/+ littermate controls, Th2a-CreER; Rab7f/f animals exhibited ~60% neuronal cell loss (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from in vivo experiments supported by Figure 3A,B.

claim: A marked reduction of P-TrkA punctae was observed in sympathetic ganglia of Th2a-CreER; Rab7f/f mice compared to Th2a-CreER; Rab7f/+ controls.
source: Interestingly, a marked reduction of P-TrkA punctae was observed in sympathetic ganglia of Th2a-CreER; Rab7f/f mice compared to Th2a-CreER; Rab7f/+ controls (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vivo experiments supported by Figure 3C.

claim: In the absence of Rab7, a decrease in both pre- and post-synaptic specializations visualized using antibodies against VAChT and Homer1 was observed.
source: Moreover, in the absence of Rab7, a decrease in both pre- and post-synaptic specializations visualized using antibodies against the vesicular acetylcholine transporter (VAChT) and Homer1, respectively, was observed (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vivo experiments supported by Figure 3C,D.

claim: Rab7 functions in sympathetic neurons in vivo to support NGF-dependent survival and synapse formation.
source: Therefore, Rab7 functions in sympathetic neurons in vivo to support NGF-dependent survival and synapse formation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from in vivo experimental findings.

claim: Retrograde TrkA signaling and survival were compromised in neurons lacking Rab7 in vitro.
source: Consistent with the in vivo analysis, retrograde TrkA signaling (Figure 3E,F) and survival (Figure 3G; Figure 3—figure supplement 1D) were compromised in neurons lacking Rab7 in vitro.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vitro experiments supported by Figure 3E,F,G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Addition of NGF directly to cell bodies and proximal axons of neurons lacking Rab7 supported their survival.

claim: Rab7 knockdown did not affect mitochondria movement in axons.

evidence: This is a control experiment supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Expression of the Rab7 shRNA in sympathetic neurons virtually abolished retrograde transport of Flag-TrkA+ endosomes.

claim: Rab7 depletion did not affect TrkA internalization in distal axons.

claim: Expression of hRab7, but not mRab7, in sympathetic neurons treated with the Rab7 shRNA restored both retrograde TrkA transport and survival.

claim: Rab7 is a general mediator of retrograde TrkA transport and survival across different neuronal types.

evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experiments in different neuronal types supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: Rab7 mediates retrograde TrkA transport and signaling both in vivo and in vitro.
source: Taken together, these findings indicate that Rab7 mediates retrograde TrkA transport and signaling both in vivo and in vitro.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: Comparable levels of Rab5+ or CD63-mCherry+ Flag-TrkA endosomes were found in neurons expressing control or Rab7 shRNA.
source: Interestingly, comparable levels of Rab5+ or CD63-mCherry+ Flag-TrkA endosomes were found in neurons expressing control or Rab7 shRNA, suggesting that Rab7 is not required for formation of TrkA EEs and MVBs in distal axons (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H–J).

claim: Rab7 is not required for formation of TrkA EEs and MVBs in distal axons.
source: Interestingly, comparable levels of Rab5+ or CD63-mCherry+ Flag-TrkA endosomes were found in neurons expressing control or Rab7 shRNA, suggesting that Rab7 is not required for formation of TrkA EEs and MVBs in distal axons (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H–J).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1H–J.

claim: RILP mediates late endosome positioning and dynein-dependent movement along microtubules.
source: We focused on one Rab7 effector protein, RILP, because it mediates late endosome positioning and dynein-dependent movement along microtubules (Jordens et al., 2001; Johansson et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: RILP-EGFP was co-localized and co-transported with retrograde Flag-TrkA endosomes in proximal axons of compartmentalized sympathetic neurons.

claim: RILP-EGFP was associated with CD63-mCherry+ Flag-TrkA endosomes in distal axons.
source: Moreover, while RILP-EGFP was associated with CD63-mCherry+ Flag-TrkA endosomes in distal axons, Rab7 depletion abolished this association, suggesting that recruitment of RILP to TrkA+ MVBs is Rab7 dependent (Figure 3—figure supplement 1K).

claim: Rab7 depletion abolished the association of RILP-EGFP with CD63-mCherry+ Flag-TrkA endosomes.
source: Moreover, while RILP-EGFP was associated with CD63-mCherry+ Flag-TrkA endosomes in distal axons, Rab7 depletion abolished this association, suggesting that recruitment of RILP to TrkA+ MVBs is Rab7 dependent (Figure 3—figure supplement 1K).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1K.

claim: Recruitment of RILP to TrkA+ MVBs is Rab7 dependent.
source: Moreover, while RILP-EGFP was associated with CD63-mCherry+ Flag-TrkA endosomes in distal axons, Rab7 depletion abolished this association, suggesting that recruitment of RILP to TrkA+ MVBs is Rab7 dependent (Figure 3—figure supplement 1K).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1K.

claim: In neurons expressing an shRNA directed against RILP, retrograde TrkA transport was markedly compromised.
source: Moreover, in neurons expressing an shRNA directed against RILP, retrograde TrkA transport was markedly compromised (Figure 3—figure supplement 1O,P).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1O,P.

claim: A Rab7-RILP module associated with TrkA MVBs mediates long-range retrograde transport of TrkA.
source: Taken together, these findings suggest a Rab7-RILP module associated with TrkA MVBs mediates long-range retrograde transport of TrkA.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: Both TrkA+ early endosomes and MVBs within axons contain P-TrkA Y490 and Y785.
source: Indeed, both TrkA+ early endosomes and MVBs within axons contain P-TrkA Y490 and Y785, indicative of an active TrkA signaling state (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by Figure 4A,B.

claim: Most TrkA+ MVBs in axons and cell bodies were observed in association with the active form of PLCγ phosphorylated on tyrosine residue 783.
source: Moreover, most TrkA+ MVBs in axons and cell bodies were observed in association with the active form of a key TrkA effector, PLCγ phosphorylated on tyrosine residue 783, suggesting an ability of TrkA MVBs to recruit and activate core TrkA signaling pathway effectors (Figure 4A,B; Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by Figure 4A,B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: TrkA MVBs have an ability to recruit and activate core TrkA signaling pathway effectors.
source: Moreover, most TrkA+ MVBs in axons and cell bodies were observed in association with the active form of a key TrkA effector, PLCγ phosphorylated on tyrosine residue 783, suggesting an ability of TrkA MVBs to recruit and activate core TrkA signaling pathway effectors (Figure 4A,B; Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data supported by Figure 4A,B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Both P-Trk and P-PLCγ were observed co-localized with retrogradely transported Flag-TrkA on the limiting membrane and intraluminal vesicles (ILVs) of MVBs in cell bodies in a K252a-dependent manner.

claim: Over 50% of CD63 punctae in both distal and proximal axons were Lamp1+.
source: While over 50% of CD63 punctae in both distal and proximal axons were Lamp1+, very few CD63/Flag-TrkA double-labeled punctae were associated with lysosomes in axons and cell bodies (8.5 ± 2.2%; Figure 4a,b; Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).

claim: Very few CD63/Flag-TrkA double-labeled punctae were associated with lysosomes in axons and cell bodies (8.5 ± 2.2%).
source: While over 50% of CD63 punctae in both distal and proximal axons were Lamp1+, very few CD63/Flag-TrkA double-labeled punctae were associated with lysosomes in axons and cell bodies (8.5 ± 2.2%; Figure 4a,b; Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding supported by Figure 4a,b and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Both TrkA+ early endosomes and MVBs recruit NGF/TrkA signaling effector proteins.
source: Taken together, both TrkA+ early endosomes and MVBs recruit NGF/TrkA signaling effector proteins, suggesting that both are capable of TrkA effector signaling, and retrograde TrkA+ MVBs are uniquely not degradative.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: Both TrkA+ early endosomes and MVBs are capable of TrkA effector signaling.
source: Taken together, both TrkA+ early endosomes and MVBs recruit NGF/TrkA signaling effector proteins, suggesting that both are capable of TrkA effector signaling, and retrograde TrkA+ MVBs are uniquely not degradative.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental findings.

claim: Retrograde TrkA+ MVBs are uniquely not degradative.
source: Taken together, both TrkA+ early endosomes and MVBs recruit NGF/TrkA signaling effector proteins, suggesting that both are capable of TrkA effector signaling, and retrograde TrkA+ MVBs are uniquely not degradative.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental findings.

claim: The majority of TrkA receptors are localized to the membrane of intraluminal vesicles (ILVs) of TrkA+ MVBs while a smaller subset is present on the MVB limiting membrane.
source: From the ultrastructural analysis of retrogradely transported Flag-TrkA+ endosomes in cell bodies, we observed that the majority of TrkA receptors are localized to the membrane of intraluminal vesicles (ILVs) of TrkA+ MVBs while a smaller subset is present on the MVB limiting membrane (Figure 1).
evidence: This is an observation from EM analysis supported by Figure 1.

claim: The topology of TrkA receptors associated with ILVs indicate that its catalytic domain and phosphotyrosine residues are located within the ILV lumen.
source: Based on principles of MVB formation (Hanson and Cashikar, 2012; Katzmann et al., 2002), previous ultrastructural studies of other RTKs (Futter et al., 1996), and our immuno-EM analysis, the topology of TrkA receptors associated with ILVs indicate that its catalytic domain and phosphotyrosine residues are located within the ILV lumen (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an inference based on established principles and experimental data supported by Figure 4D.

claim: TrkA receptors in ILVs are presumably unable to transmit NGF pro-survival signaling cascades to the cytoplasm and nucleus due to the restricted localization of their effector domains.
source: TrkA receptors in such a configuration are presumably unable to transmit NGF pro-survival signaling cascades to the cytoplasm and nucleus due to the restricted localization of their effector domains.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the topology of TrkA receptors in ILVs.

claim: TrkA receptors on the limiting membrane are in a signaling accessible position with their signaling domains facing the cytoplasm.
source: TrkA receptors on the limiting membrane, in contrast, are in a signaling accessible position with their signaling domains facing the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is an inference based on membrane topology principles.

claim: The blockade of retrograde transport in distal axons by nocodazole was highly effective since it completely blocked accumulation of newly formed Flag-TrkA endosomes within the cell body compartment.
source: The blockade of retrograde transport in distal axons by nocodazole was highly effective since it completely blocked accumulation of newly formed Flag-TrkA endosomes within the cell body compartment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a validation of the experimental method supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Nocodazole treatment at 25 min post-NGF application to distal axons resulted in sparse accumulation of retrograde TrkA endosomes in cell bodies at the 1 hr time point post-NGF treatment.
source: Moreover, nocodazole treatment at 25 min post-NGF application to distal axons resulted in sparse accumulation of retrograde TrkA endosomes in cell bodies at the 1 hr time point post-NGF treatment and a relatively low, but stable number of TrkA receptors were observed over the subsequent several hours (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by Figure 5B.

claim: Neurons without axonal transport blockade exhibited a dramatic increase in the number of retrograde Flag-TrkA+ vesicles appearing in cell bodies during the 1 hr time period.
source: In contrast, neurons without axonal transport blockade exhibited a dramatic increase in the number of retrograde Flag-TrkA+ vesicles appearing in cell bodies during the 1 hr time period (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by Figure 5B.

claim: Nocodazole application to distal axons did not affect microtubule-dependent endosome maturation and trafficking within the cell body compartment.
source: Furthermore, nocodazole application to distal axons did not affect microtubule-dependent endosome maturation and trafficking within the cell body compartment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D,E), indicating effective compartmentalization of transport blockade.
evidence: This is a control finding supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1D,E.

claim: Any change in TrkA+ endosome ultrastructure in cell bodies at times following addition of nocodazole to distal axons is the result of maturation or evolution of existing endosomes that had arrived prior to nocodazole application.
source: These findings indicate that any change in TrkA+ endosome ultrastructure in cell bodies at times following addition of nocodazole to distal axons is the result of maturation or evolution of existing endosomes that had arrived prior to nocodazole application, and not newly trafficked endosomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pulse-block experimental design.

claim: 1 hr after NGF application to distal axons, and following blockade of newly arriving endosomes, the majority (92.8 ± 3.6%) of retrograde TrkA+ endosomes were MVBs.
source: Consistent with our previous experiments, 1 hr after NGF application to distal axons, and following blockade of newly arriving endosomes, the majority (92.8 ± 3.6%) of retrograde TrkA+ endosomes were MVBs (Figure 5E, left panel).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the pulse-block EM experiment supported by Figure 5E.

claim: Among the MVB-resident TrkA receptors, 68.3 ± 2.6% were localized to ILVs and 24.5 ± 4.7% to the limiting membrane.
source: Among the MVB-resident TrkA receptors, 68.3 ± 2.6% were localized to ILVs and 24.5 ± 4.7% to the limiting membrane (Figure 5E, right panel).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the pulse-block EM experiment supported by Figure 5E.

claim: The fraction of total cell body Flag punctae found associated with MVBs decreased during the next several hours.
source: Strikingly, the fraction of total cell body Flag punctae found associated with MVBs decreased during the next several hours, and this decrease was coincident with the emergence of Flag-TrkA+ SVs, which peaked (42.4 ± 8.2%) at ~5 hr post-NGF treatment (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the pulse-block EM experiment supported by Figure 5E.

claim: The emergence of Flag-TrkA+ SVs peaked (42.4 ± 8.2%) at ~5 hr post-NGF treatment.
source: Strikingly, the fraction of total cell body Flag punctae found associated with MVBs decreased during the next several hours, and this decrease was coincident with the emergence of Flag-TrkA+ SVs, which peaked (42.4 ± 8.2%) at ~5 hr post-NGF treatment (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the pulse-block EM experiment supported by Figure 5E.

claim: The fraction of Flag-TrkA+ puncta associated with lysosomes remained low during the first 8 hr of blocking the arrival of new endosomes.
source: Moreover, the fraction of Flag-TrkA+ puncta associated with lysosomes remained low during the first 8 hr of blocking the arrival of new endosomes, and by 24 hr post-NGF the majority of Flag-TrkA receptors were found associated with lysosomes (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the pulse-block EM experiment supported by Figure 5E.

claim: By 24 hr post-NGF the majority of Flag-TrkA receptors were found associated with lysosomes.
source: Moreover, the fraction of Flag-TrkA+ puncta associated with lysosomes remained low during the first 8 hr of blocking the arrival of new endosomes, and by 24 hr post-NGF the majority of Flag-TrkA receptors were found associated with lysosomes (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the pulse-block EM experiment supported by Figure 5E.

claim: The Flag-TrkA+ SVs are derived, either directly or indirectly, from TrkA+ MVBs.
source: Because the transport blockade prevented TrkA+ endosomes from entering cell bodies in this pulse-block paradigm, the most parsimonious explanation of the source of the TrkA+ SV population during the course of these experiments is that they emerge de novo within cell bodies. Since the vast majority of newly arrived Flag-TrkA+ endosomes at the start of the transport blockade are MVBs, the Flag-TrkA+ SVs are therefore derived, either directly or indirectly, from TrkA+ MVBs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pulse-block experimental design and data.

claim: The membrane localization of retrogradely transported TrkA changes following TrkA+ endosome entry into the cell body.
source: These observations indicate that the membrane localization of retrogradely transported TrkA, and indeed the ultrastructural properties of TrkA+ endosomes, changes following TrkA+ endosome entry into the cell body.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pulse-block EM data.

claim: The majority of newly internalized transferrin and Flag-TrkA were co-localized within distal axons.
source: The majority of newly internalized transferrin and Flag-TrkA were co-localized within distal axons, suggesting that they can be sorted into the same early endosomes (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The level of co-localization between transferrin and Flag-TrkA decreased over time.
source: Interestingly, the level of co-localization decreased over time, indicating that these cargoes were later sorted into different vesicular compartments (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Retrogradely transported Flag-TrkA and transferrin remained segregated upon their arrival into cell bodies.
source: Moreover, retrogradely transported Flag-TrkA and transferrin remained segregated upon their arrival into cell bodies (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Retrogradely transported transferrin and TrkA were localized to distinct MVBs.
source: Consistent with this, in EM experiments in which transferrin and Flag-TrkA were labeled with different size gold particles, we found that retrogradely transported transferrin and TrkA were localized to distinct MVBs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from EM supported by Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claim: SVs containing transferrin were not observed in cell bodies.
source: In addition, in contrast to the observed emergence of TrkA+ SVs in cell bodies, we did not observe SVs containing transferrin (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from EM supported by Figure 5F.

evidence: This is an experimental finding from the pulse-block EM experiment.

claim: Transferrin and TrkA are retrogradely transported in distinct MVBs populations.
source: Therefore, transferrin and TrkA are retrogradely transported in distinct MVBs populations, and TrkA+ MVBs are unique in that they give rise to SVs and evade lysosomal fusion.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: TrkA+ MVBs are unique in that they give rise to SVs and evade lysosomal fusion.
source: Therefore, transferrin and TrkA are retrogradely transported in distinct MVBs populations, and TrkA+ MVBs are unique in that they give rise to SVs and evade lysosomal fusion.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: Flag-TrkA receptors localized to the membrane of SVs were observed co-localized with P-TrkA and P-PLCγ 5 hr following NGF application to distal axons.

claim: TrkA+ SVs derived from MVBs are signaling competent and capable of transducing TrkA signals within the cell body.

claim: The majority of newly internalized Flag-TrkA receptors are associated with APEX2-Rab5+ endosomes (67.9 ± 7.2%).

claim: Very few Flag-TrkA punctae were found to be associated with APEX2-Rab5+ structures at the 5 hr time point of the pulse-block Flag-TrkA assay (6.4 ± 2.0%).
source: In contrast, and consistent with our immunocytochemical analyses, very few Flag-TrkA punctae were found to be associated with APEX2-Rab5+ structures at the 5 hr time point of the pulse-block Flag-TrkA assay (6.4 ± 2.0%; Figure 6C, right; Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from APEX2-EM supported by Figure 6C and Figure 6E.

claim: TrkA+ SVs that emerge from MVBs in cell bodies are not associated with Rab5.

claim: At the 5 hr time point of the pulse-block Flag-TrkA assay, Flag-TrkA+ endosomes were associated with Rab11 (13.0 ± 6.6%).

source: Therefore, a substantial portion of TrkA+ SVs exhibit a molecular feature of retromer complexes, and a subset may include Rab11+ recycling endosomes.

claim: Exposure of Flag-TrkB/A-F592A infected neurons to BDNF in the absence of NGF was sufficient to promote the generation and transport of Flag-TrkB/A-F592A+ signaling endosomes.

claim: In cells expressing Flag-TrkB/A-F592A and treated with 1NMPP1 applied to their cell bodies, there was a dramatic increase in Lamp1+ Flag endosomes compared to the three control conditions.

claim: TrkA kinase signaling in cell bodies prevents precocious sorting of retrograde TrkA+ endosomes to lysosomes.

claim: At later time points, neurons exposed to 1NMPP1 on cell bodies exhibited a much lower fraction of Flag-TrkB/A-F592A+ MVBs, virtually no Flag-TrkB/A-F592A+ SVs, and a much higher percentage of Flag-TrkB/A-F592A+ lysosomes, compared to DMSO control-treated neurons.
source: However, at later time points, neurons exposed to 1NMPP1 on cell bodies exhibited a much lower fraction of Flag-TrkB/A-F592A+ MVBs, virtually no Flag-TrkB/A-F592A+ SVs, and a much higher percentage of Flag-TrkB/A-F592A+ lysosomes, compared to DMSO control-treated neurons (Figure 7B,C).

claim: NGF application to the cell body compartment partially rescued premature lysosome sorting of retrograde Flag-TrkB/A-F592A+ MVBs in neurons treated with 1NMPP1 applied to the cell bodies.

claim: NGF application directly to cell bodies did not prevent the rapid sorting of retrogradely transported transferrin-containing endosomes to lysosomes.

claim: The fate of retrogradely transported MVBs within cell bodies is dependent on the nature and signaling activity of its cargo.
source: Thus, the fate of retrogradely transported MVBs within cell bodies is dependent on the nature and signaling activity of its cargo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: TrkA kinase signaling promotes the emergence of TrkA+ SVs from TrkA+ MVBs and protects or delays these endosomes from acquiring a lysosomal fate.
source: TrkA kinase signaling promotes the emergence of TrkA+ SVs from TrkA+ MVBs and protects or delays these endosomes from acquiring a lysosomal fate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the chemical genetic experiments.

claim: TrkA receptors can signal in trans to influence the fate of retrograde TrkA+ signaling endosomes and prevent their lysosomal targeting and degradation.
source: Moreover, TrkA receptors can signal in trans, albeit to a lesser extent than endosomal TrkA signals acting in cis, to influence the fate of retrograde TrkA+ signaling endosomes and prevent their lysosomal targeting and degradation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the NGF rescue experiments.

claim: Endosomal TrkA signals acting in cis are more effective than TrkA signals acting in trans at influencing the fate of retrograde TrkA+ signaling endosomes.
source: Moreover, TrkA receptors can signal in trans, albeit to a lesser extent than endosomal TrkA signals acting in cis, to influence the fate of retrograde TrkA+ signaling endosomes and prevent their lysosomal targeting and degradation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the effects of cis versus trans TrkA signaling.
